HOW THE TESTS ARE BUILT (additions to the design text; none weakens a check)
- Every failure row runs all of A1-A6 (K1-K4 for the SIGKILL rows) and fails at the end naming every check that failed (the checks() collector of helpers.js), so a row on the pre-fix code shows which checks it breaks. Each CLI run is a separate node process with a 10 s timeout (also mkfifo, the socket maker and the child listings), stderr is compared line by line, and the strict listing (types, modes, sizes, sha256, file mtimes in ns, link text; folder mtimes not compared) is compared before and after; after the obstacle and the named leftovers are removed an in-process applyVerdict/prepareRun with the same arguments must converge to the clean bytes (A6).
- States RF/RR/EF are built per test (RR = a clean application, then one stale line after the block heading and one \n appended to proposed-actions.json and apply-report.json); every file of an apply fixture gets the modification time 2000-01-01, so 'not touched' and 'the same file' show in the listing whatever the clock resolution is (my addition). Clean bytes come from an in-process applyVerdict/prepareRun once per test file: RF 1066/353/419 B and run.json 1035 B, equal to the design's measures.
- W53 and P18 wrap fs.openSync as well as fsyncSync and renameSync (mock.method, mock.restoreAll in finally) to learn which file each fsync belongs to; they check the exact count and the order.
- W51 takes its two strict listings in a child process with a time limit (listingInChild): with a pipe in the root, a tree() that opened it would freeze the whole test file instead of failing a row. I found it with the design's mutant M16d (before the change that mutant froze apply.write.test.js; now W51, W52 and L09 fail).
- W34 asserts its own premise (new STATE.md > 2 KiB, the two other targets < 512 B) so it cannot fail for a wrong reason.
- fault-inject.js follows the 9.2 contract: 8 methods, the 6 effects throw/partial/kill/partial-kill/preempt/bug, fields fn/paths/from/to/nth/effect/code, each fault fires once; a broken SAI_TEST_FAULTS throws at load so a fault cannot silently never fire. nth is implemented as the contract says; no designed row uses it.
- The two edits of existing tests: cli.test.js ('unreadable verdict-1.md') and validate.run.test.js (unreadable copy) put back the mode they read with fs.statSync instead of the literal 0o644. Verified: with the strict tree the original cli test fails under umask 077 (0600 -> 0644), with the edit it passes. The tree() callers (apply.accept, apply.reject, apply.state, cli) compare strings and need no edit.
- Files (sha256 prefix): apply.write.test.js ec63f01ca85a865a, prepare.write.test.js be0b9a8b51b3dd51, listing.test.js 5bca08232a3db805, fault-inject.js a6649220c74667a5, helpers.js c4cc1689100fb4f8, cli.test.js e45cdb47eb2574ab, validate.run.test.js 1b158f6315446394.

Proposed rows for a design round: (a) W55 RR: linkSync STATE.md -> .STATE.md.sai-old throws EEXIST (a race), expected 'E_WRITE STATE.md: leftover .STATE.md.sai-old from an interrupted or concurrent run (EEXIST); nothing was changed; if no other command is running, delete and re-run' (needs no change of the fault contract); (b) P19: mkdirSync of runs/.WF06-20260925-01.sai-tmp throws EEXIST, expected 'E_WRITE runs/WF06-20260925-01: leftover runs/.WF06-20260925-01.sai-tmp ...'; (c) a W46 variant with two failing removals after the commit, both named (X4); (d) a program error that carries a string code but no syscall (as Node's own ERR_* errors do) must not become E_WRITE (X1): needs a new fault effect, i.e. a change of the 9.2 contract; (e) two message variants have no row: 'could not remove this backup of the old version' and 'rollback failed ... it was created by this run and is still there'. I did not add these rows: they are not in the validated design and adding rows is a design decision.
2. Design 9.2/9.6/9.7 treat a tree() that opens pipes as dangerous only for L09. In fact any row that has a pipe in the root and lists it in the test process (W51) freezes its whole file under such a tree(). W51 now lists in a child; suggest one sentence in 9.2 and in M16 ('opens a pipe and a socket' -> L09, W51, W52 as observed).
3. Candidate anti-pattern for DOC-UPDATER (Q13): a measuring tool that can hang must not be run in the test process of a row that feeds it the hanging input (found here through mutant M16d).
4. The Sai-delta items Q8 (shop A cannot see or change shop B) and Q11 (a shop-supplied internal URL is rejected) have no test: design 10 and 12 mark them not applicable (no shop data, no URL, no network in tools/). Q10 'each external call failing' is realised as one injected failure per OS call of the write phase (the W and P rows). This is not a lowering of the bar: there is nothing to test for those two items here.
5. Design 9.7 gives the application of the mutants to the TEST-DESIGNER; this handoff gave it to the TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR. I ran them anyway (above); the harness stayed in the scratch folder.
6. Running on a bare copy of tools/ (as 9.7 does) makes the four repo.test.js tests fail because there is no repo around it; the other 193 tests are unaffected.
